newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close up sharply to limit.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close up sharply to limit.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply higher to limit up on bargain hunting, short covering and buy stops, traders said.
May closed limit up at $383.30 while other months ended $9.90 to $2.70 higher. March finished up $9.60 at $411.40.

Futures rallied sharply after initial carryover sell stops lacked followthrough and short covering developed. Bargain hunting was evident, especially when the Random Lengths quote price for spruce was not as low as had been anticipated. Spreading of long May/short March added to strength in May, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $414 per tbf, down $2 from midweek but still $1 up from last Friday.
Futures went against technicals to post gains. The market had looked very weak after tumbling about $28 per tbf earlier in the week, they said.

"Lumber has had a real tendency to crack the main trend lines and then come right back into the pattern - I think we are doing that right now," said Curt Cunningham, President Pacific Futures Trading.
